title: A divisor sum over shifted squares is always a multiple of 4
summary: For N = 16n + 6, the sum of σ₀(N − k²) over 1 ≤ k < √N is divisible by 4.
source: S. Jirattikansakul, T. Kittipassorn, K. Kongsiri, N. Moonwichit, K. Sriamorn, "Congruences via Partitions with Exactly Two Part Sizes", arXiv:2604.25394v1 (28 April 2026), first conjecture of the concluding remarks.
label: lean
first_by: Qianghao Wu, `KenWuqianghao/kenwu-lab`, folder `results/square-plus-product-divisors` (Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24580854): a public Lean proof of a stronger statement (every N that leaves remainder 6 when divided by 8), first committed on 27 November 2026 at 01:44 UTC and released that morning. The proof here was checked on 26 November, about fourteen hours earlier, and the two were found independently; but the proof here was not public then, so theirs is the first published proof.
